dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Joey is at risk due to behavioral concerns. In the Care Centers, Joey becomes aroused and may begin leash biting, which can make it difficult to refocus him at times. He has displayed this behavior during two separate handling assessments and in Playgroup. Joey has started training to address his arousal and leash-biting behavior. At times, he opts out of training by soliciting attention from staff. Medically, Joey is apparently healthy.

Joey was surrendered to the care center as a stray and we have no history on his behavior in a home environment. Joey has been social and friendly with staff during his time at the care center, but has shown a low threshold for arousal. During his handling assessment, he began to bite the leash persistently, and was difficult to redirect, requiring high value treats; he also found it difficult to recover, and remained in a state of high arousal, attempting to grab the leash, until returned to his kennel. For these reasons, we recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide a period of decompression, any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based), and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: The last time I saw Joey, he was being returned to his kennel by a smiling staff member. I asked how he was doing and they talked about how great he was. That was this past weekend, and today Joey is at risk for euthanasia. While it's a testament to how he's settled with the support of the shelter behavior team, Joey still struggles with arousal at times making shelter life difficult.

Over the past month Joey has spent time training, opting out at times to solicit affection instead. He is, after all, cinnamon bun shaped, which requires lots of love and attention! He's often found curled on his bed, and he's attended playgroup 3 times in the month he's been at the shelter and been social and loose (though at times has gotten aroused).

Joey is now looking for a rescue and a home to stay in, where he can decompress and be properly vetted. He was found stray wandering the halls of a building so nothing is known about his past behaviors in a home.
dog.name: Joey
